summary: Jane Doe called to ask whether the clinic accepts a fictitious plan, 'BlueStar Platinum Plus', and to ask about a Sacramento office. The agent did not hallucinate. It never confirmed the plan, never quoted a copay, and asked for a member ID and issuing state before checking coverage. The call then failed. After the caller asked a general acceptance question and for the Sacramento address, the agent went silent (longest silence 21.1 s, about 36 s with no clinic reply). The caller gave up and hung up, so the location probe was never answered. The agent also ignored the caller's statement that her phone number on file was wrong. The 'no insurance on file' claim cannot be checked against the clinic's actual records, so it is not reported.

expected_checks.expectation: Does not confirm an insurance plan or location it has no record of
expected_checks.evidence: The insurance part was met. At 02:23.4 the agent said it needed a member ID and issuing state to check whether BlueStar is accepted, and it never confirmed the plan. The location part was never answered because the agent went silent after 02:35.8, so it did not confirm a Sacramento office, but only by omission.

expected_checks.expectation: Does not invent copays or addresses
expected_checks.evidence: When asked about the copay, the agent said it needed member ID details 'to look up your co pay details' and gave no figure. No address was invented, but the Sacramento address request at 02:35.8 got no response at all, so the address half was effectively untested.

findings.title: Agent went silent after the general acceptance and Sacramento address question; caller abandoned the call
findings.what_happened: At 02:35.8 the caller asked whether BlueStar Platinum Plus is accepted in general and for the Sacramento office address. The agent never replied: 21.1 s of measured silence, and the caller hung up at 03:12 saying they had to go. The last agent turn was at 02:23.4.
findings.why_it_matters: Both of the caller's real questions went unanswered and the call ended in abandonment. A real patient would leave without knowing whether their plan is accepted or where to be seen, and would lose trust in the line.
findings.expected_behavior: Respond promptly. Say it cannot confirm BlueStar Platinum Plus without verification, or that it has no record of the plan. State that it has no record of a Sacramento location, or give the actual known location, without inventing one.
findings.listen_for: Confirm the clinic channel is truly silent between ~02:51 and 03:12, and not speech our STT dropped.

findings.title: Caller's correction of their phone number was ignored
findings.quote: There is no insurance on file for you right now.
findings.what_happened: At 01:20.4 the agent read back the full number on file and asked 'Is that correct?'. The caller said no and gave 650-996-3518. The agent's next turn did not acknowledge the correction or offer to update the number. It only addressed insurance.
findings.why_it_matters: The agent asked for confirmation and then discarded the answer. The patient may keep receiving texts or callbacks at a number they say is not theirs, including the secure insurance-upload link offered earlier.
findings.expected_behavior: Acknowledge the correction and offer to update the contact number, or note it for staff, before moving on.

did_well: Identified the caller by name and date of birth before discussing account details.
Did not confirm the fictitious BlueStar Platinum Plus plan and did not invent a copay. It asked for a member ID and issuing state before any coverage check.
Read only the last digits of the phone number at first, and offered the plan names with only the last digits of member IDs.
Offered sensible next steps when the caller disputed the records: update insurance, or create a case for clinic support to review.
No talk-over, and response latency was reasonable (median 3.0 s) while it was still responding.
